projects.title: Graph Cinema
projects.tagline: A downstream runtime that makes governed graph motion, alternate trajectories, protected dissent, and continuity receipts inspectable.
projects.story: Graph Cinema is the runtime and visualization layer within the larger Agentic Graphfield Engineering program. Agentic Graphfield Engineering is the engineering discipline; Parallax Graphfield Dynamics is the formal theory of governed rewrites, constraints, trajectories, and counterfactuals; Graph Cinema is the ledgered motion picture formed by successive graph frames and the decisions between them. Publication Pack 1 makes that hierarchy, its constitutional boundary, and a first deterministic comparison proof publicly inspectable.
projects.summary: A graph is one frame. A graphfield is the governed world producing frames. A trajectory is the motion picture through admissible states, while the ledger preserves the packets, judgments, authority, dissent, rewrites, receipts, and replay manifest that explain why motion occurred—or why it was blocked.
projects.see: The AGE/PGD/Graph Cinema hierarchy, graphfield and trajectory map, canonical office-judgment track, Phase 0 constitutional artifacts, the deterministic repair-versus-direct viewer, and the existing PAT Mk.1 Graph Mode.
projects.proof: Seven public artifacts are connected: three reviewed SVG visuals, two source-led public briefs, one standalone deterministic trajectory viewer, and the live PAT Mk.1 Graph Mode integration. The standalone viewer uses fixed hand-authored data and no model calls. The canonical source DOCX files remain retained rather than silently replaced.
projects.next: Freeze a shell-neutral signed trajectory fixture and connect the viewer to canonical packet, judgment, authority, rewrite, dissent, receipt, and frame objects without allowing the visualization layer to mutate them. Then test deterministic replay across two independent implementations.
projects.claimBoundary: Graph Cinema is a runtime and visualization architecture, not the source of canonical truth. The published deterministic viewer proves browser playback, stepping, comparison, preserved dissent, and fixed-data replay. It does not prove graph reasoning, model independence, optimal governance, cryptographic integrity, or correctness of generated judgments. A visualization may never authorize a rewrite or replace a complete receipt.
